data.value: The cause is in `dayKey`: it uses local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`) while its contract — the comment "groups events by calendar day in UTC" and the test name "day keys are UTC days" — requires UTC. Under `TZ=America/New_York`, `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` falls on Jan 1 local time, so it returns `2026-01-01`.

part.text:
The cause is in `dayKey`: it uses local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`) while its contract — the comment "groups events by calendar day in UTC" and the test name "day keys are UTC days" — requires UTC. Under `TZ=America/New_York`, `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` falls on Jan 1 local time, so it returns `2026-01-01`.Fixed. The timezone test passes; the other two failures are separate pre-existing bugs (a CLI flag not coerced to number, and a missing null guard in `format.js`) — let me know if you want those fixed too.

**Cause:** `dayKey` in `packages/shared/src/dates.js` used the local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`) while its contract (the "calendar day in UTC" comment and the test name) requires UTC. Setting `process.env.TZ = "America/New_York"` in the test made `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` land on Jan 1 in local time, producing `2026-01-01` instead of `2026-01-02`.

**Fix:** switched to `getUTCFullYear`/`getUTCMonth`/`getUTCDate`, making the output independent of the process timezone.

Note: `dayKey` had no other callers in the repo, so no other code depends on the old local-time behavior.
